headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can ingest and exfiltrate ComfyUI-generated content via broad network/MCP paths, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no MCP, clipboard, or browser surface, so it is not a direct injection source. next-ai-draw-io uses browsers and MCP and can consume external content, so if ComfyUI outputs are copied into its workflow, prompt-like text embedded in diagrams or documents could steer it. The pathway is interaction-based, not default, so medium fits.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are manually pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts or diagram text fields
IF next-ai-draw-io parses imported document text as instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of model-generated text into prompts
Use a fixed template that strips instruction-like text
Review imported diagram/document text before AI processing
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, workflows, seeds, and model assets locally, while next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress, browser access, MCP, and API-key handling. If ComfyUI artifacts are moved into next-ai-draw-io, the latter can transmit them to third-party model APIs by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive work products.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs or model assets are imported into next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io routes those inputs to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive ComfyUI outputs out of next-ai-draw-io
Select a local-only backend in next-ai-draw-io
Block outbound network access for the diagram tool
Rotate or remove API keys from the diagram tool
requires-engineering: enforce per-project data egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with next-ai-draw-io in the usual way. next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and uses MCP, but the pair lacks overlapping write surfaces in the profiles. Any conflict would require unusual external orchestration, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable workspace
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to edit shared files while ComfyUI is also active
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Avoid shared git repositories for generated artifacts
Run only one writer at a time
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can treat imported text, PDFs, or diagrams as AI-assisted inputs, so ComfyUI-generated captions, prompts, or metadata may be accepted as authoritative without verification. ComfyUI itself does not act downstream, but its outputs can become inputs to a more action-oriented document workflow, creating a plausible cascade in default use.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated text or metadata is imported into next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io renders or acts on that content without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review before acting on imported content
Separate generated captions from source facts
Mark AI-generated fields as untrusted
Use a verification checklist before export
requires-engineering: add source-citation enforcement

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as fully offline and local, while next-ai-draw-io explicitly calls remote APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure OpenAI, and others, and handles API keys. If regulated or sensitive documents are moved from the local image workflow into the document tool, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive content from ComfyUI is processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io sends that content to a non-local API provider
mitigations: Use only local models in next-ai-draw-io
Do not process regulated data in the diagram tool
Review retention settings for each API provider
Store API keys outside shared project files
requires-engineering: document data-residency boundaries
